concepts.prompt: Game pickup item concept: ONE single wrapped hard sweet candy lying on its side, the classic bow-tie candy-wrapper silhouette: a plump rounded oval sweet in the middle with the wrapper twisted tight at both ends and fanning out into two crinkled flared wrapper tails. Premium wrapper: rich sky-to-royal blue body with polished metallic silver bands and silver foil twisted tails, a small embossed silver star on the front, glossy foil sheen with a few subtle tiny white sparkle glints. The underside is slightly flattened so it rests flat on the ground. Same family and finish as the wrapped gold candies in the first reference (chunky soft-bevelled forms, hand-painted PBR look) but only one sweet: no cloth, no pile. Stylised Palworld-like game prop, chunky readable silhouette that reads clearly from far away, about 0.25 m long. Single isolated object, centred, three-quarter elevated view, plain neutral grey background, even studio lighting, no text, no logos, no characters, no ground. Strictly no red, pink, maroon or oxblood anywhere.
references: tb/meshy-props assets/props/meshy-1020/candy_pickup_set/model_candy_rare/preview_3view.png (middle 3/4 panel cropped (360,0)-(720,360), upscaled 2x; local derived file rare_34.png): the published rare_candy pickup, judged 6.90, used as family style reference

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MJohnsonWellabe/Tetherbound/main/docs/reference/tetherbound-meadows-keyart.png (downscaled to 1024 px; local derived file keyart_small.png): Meadows palette and finish
concepts.verdict: rejected: correct colours and an embossed silver star, but every view stood the sweet upright (or tilted on a diagonal) and the body was a taller egg shape than good_candy, so it would not share the form or lie flat

concepts.prompt: Game pickup item concept: ONE single wrapped hard sweet candy lying HORIZONTALLY on its side, exactly the same shape, proportions and bow-tie silhouette as the green candy in the first reference (plump rounded oval sweet in the middle, wrapper twisted tight at both ends, two crinkled flared wrapper tails pointing left and right), shown as the premium tier of the same candy family. Chunky soft-bevelled forms and hand-painted PBR finish like the wrapped candies in the second reference, but only one sweet: no cloth, no pile. Stylised Palworld-like game prop, chunky readable silhouette that reads clearly from far away, about 0.25 m long. Single isolated object, centred, seen from a three-quarter elevated angle with the candy lying flat, plain neutral grey background, even studio lighting, no text, no logos, no characters, no ground. concepts.verdict: CHOSEN (views 0 front with star and 1 end as multi-image input; view 2 is the starless back): generated with the good_candy concept as shape reference, so it is the same lying bow-tie sweet; sky-to-royal blue body, two silver bands, embossed silver star, silver foil tails, a few white sparkle glints

reference_inspection: All references inspected before any prompt was written: the published candy_pickup_set rare preview (3-view; the gold wrapped sweets on a cream cloth with a star candy), the good/great candy previews from the same set, the rare/good/great candy UI icons (assets/ui/icons/items: gold star sweet, plain green sweet, blue star sweet) and the Meadows key art. Prompts kept the wrapped-sweet finish of the rare set but asked for one sweet only (no cloth, no pile), so the new pickups read as single items of the same family; the UI icon colour coding (green = good, blue with star = great) was followed.
